WASHINGTON: US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said.

The strait, through which a fifth of the world’s oil passes, has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the war. Iran wants relief from a blockade that is strangling its economy; Washington wants free passage restored for ships on the vital oil route that Tehran has kept closed.

Talks are complicated by a familiar diplomatic problem: neither side wants to move first.

Two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomats said the most workable option now on the table was a staged arrangement — Iran allowing ships through Hormuz in return for an end to the blockade and, potentially, access to frozen assets.

“One way forward would be to solve the crisis in stages. The first would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz,” a senior Iranian official said on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

Such a deal would require Donald Trump to accept another interim arrangement, after a previous understanding collapsed in July. The US president has suggested a fuller agreement might only be reached after November’s midterm elections. A senior European official said Iranian negotiators arrived in New York “with a very long list of demands”.

The White House, for its part, has shown little urgency. “Iran is desperate for a deal, President Trump holds all the cards and will make whatever decision is best for the United States,” a White House official said, adding that “crushing sanctions” and “one of the most successful blockades in history” had left Tehran “completely broke”.

Trump, the official suggested, was content to let an “inevitable Iranian collapse” continue rather than be rushed into concessions.

Dennis Ross, a former US negotiator, put the chances of a deal before the midterms at roughly 30 per cent, though he noted both sides had reasons to want an agreement sooner rather than later.

“The blockade is what’s really squeezing the Iranians. It’s strangling them,” he said. A pre-election deal could suit Trump too, easing Gulf tensions and helping bring down petrol prices at home. After the vote, Ross said, the president may feel freer to escalate pressure or consider military options.

Tehran, meanwhile, is hedging. Even as it explores a diplomatic exit, Iran is preparing for the possibility of renewed conflict, accusing Washington of using the blockade and the threat of force as instruments of coercion.

“Our fingers are on the trigger,” the senior Iranian official said. “The Americans know what they need to do but, because of their excessive demands, the chances of diplomacy resolving this are extremely low.”

Regional sources said Iran was prepared to drop, or at least set aside, its demand for transit fees on shipping through Hormuz in order to prioritise ending the blockade.

“Iran is not primarily focused on imposing tolls in Hormuz but on preserving its administrative control of the waterway,” the senior official said. “Iran may be willing to defer the toll issue, but they are not going to give up administrative control of the strait.”

At the heart of the diplomacy in New York is a fundamental tension. Washington wants pressure to produce concessions, Tehran wants pressure removed before making them, and the Gulf states want the conflict resolved without allowing the region’s strategic waterways to become enduring bargaining chips.

In a separate meeting in New York, Gulf leaders pressed Trump for clarity on his strategy beyond the midterms, including whether Washington would resume military action if Iran refused to negotiate.

They made clear their rejection of any Iranian control over Hormuz, insisting freedom of navigation be restored and that the strait must not become a tool of coercion — while also urging de-escalation, reflecting Gulf states’ desire to stay out of further confrontation.

“It’s still not clear what Trump’s endgame is, or what the alternative to the pressure campaign would be,” said Ebtessam al-Ketbi, president of the Emirates Policy Center in Abu Dhabi.

“The Iranians, by contrast, know what they want. They’re reshaping the regional landscape through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb with a clear objective, while Washington has yet to define its roadmap.”

Alan Eyre, another former US negotiator, warned that the blockade’s pressure could backfire: rather than softening its position, he said, Tehran was more likely to escalate, believing that any sign of weakness would prove fatal to the regime.

Adding to the diplomatic pressure, a coalition of 80 countries called at the UN on Thursday for the full restoration of maritime navigation in the Gulf.

“We call for the full restoration of navigational rights and principles without delay,” said Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid al-Zayani, reading a joint statement to journalists.

UAE suspends Iranian airline flights

In a further sign of tightening pressure, the United Arab Emirates announced on Thursday that it would no longer accept flights operated by Iranian carriers, aligning itself with US sanctions targeting Iran’s aviation sector.

Dubai has long been a key destination for Iranian airlines, serving multiple daily flights and a large Iranian community with close business ties to the emirate.

The UAE’s General Civil Aviation Authority said the suspension was “based on the US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines preventing them from using airports around the world”.

The UAE, which was hit by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones early in the war, suspended trade and financial exchanges with Iran last month.

On Wednesday its central bank blocked transactions with Iran’s Bank Melli, citing breaches of money-laundering, terrorism-financing and arms-proliferation rules.

One passenger told AFP an Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before departure on Thursday, after tickets had already been issued.

Washington imposed sanctions on Iran’s aviation sector in early September, giving airlines until Wednesday to comply — including by halting the refuelling of Iranian aircraft — or risk being cut off from the dollar-based financial system.

Iran’s main carriers were forced to cancel international flights this week as neighbouring states adopted similar restrictions; Turkmenistan turned back a flight from Tehran to Dushanbe on Thursday, an Iranian aviation official said, because it had not authorised the airline to fly.

A handful of smaller Iranian carriers continue to operate abroad, notably to Armenia and to China, which has declined to follow Washington’s sanctions.

news.title: Allies unite behind Saudi Arabia as Houthis step up attacks
news.text:
RIYADH/CAIRO: Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan will hold an urgent, high-level meeting under a joint defense pact to discuss ways to support the Kingdom amid attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, while Tehran sought to distance itself from the rapid advance of its Houthi allies.

The Houthis have launched strikes on the UN-recognized government in Yemen and repeatedly fired into Saudi Arabia, disrupting oil flows from the world’s largest energy exporter, as part of a wider Middle East war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

The Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets on Thursday, while authorities in Saudi Arabia said they had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis.

Saudi Arabia earlier issued emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Makkah, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red Sea oil port.

Saudi Arabia’s top religious authority called on soldiers in the Kingdom to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Houthis until the group is ousted from power, a statement posted by the Saudi state news agency said.

Three-way defense pact

Amid the fighting, the Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework of the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, according to a Saudi Foreign Ministry statement. They condemned attacks targeting Makkah and other civilian sites while affirming Saudi Arabia’s right to defend itself, the statement said.

“The ministers also discussed arrangements for holding an urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries to discuss ways to support Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, which stipulates that an attack against any one of the parties constitutes an attack against all parties,” the statement said.

The meeting was announced shortly after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sought to distance Iran from the Houthis in an American television interview on Thursday.

“The Houthis are responsible for their own actions,” Pezeshkian told the Fox News program “Special Report with Bret Baier,” a day after he appeared before the UN General Assembly in New York.

Tehran seeks distance from Houthis

The Pezeshkian interview and speech took place amid a pause in fighting between the US and Iran and a brief attempt at diplomacy in New York, with Qatar serving as intermediary between the warring parties.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters on Thursday that Tehran had conveyed a proposal to the United States via intermediaries under which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened if Tehran’s conditions were met.

Under Iran’s proposal, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, within seven days. The United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release its frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, he said.

“The Strait of Hormuz will be reopened on the last day,” Araqchi said, adding that talks with the United States on other issues, including Iran’s nuclear issue, would then start.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Tehran was reviewing Washington’s response to its peace proposals.

War disrupts regional energy flows

The war, which US President Donald Trump launched alongside Israel in February, has killed thousands of people and disrupted global energy supplies, pushing up oil prices.

While the US and Iran have largely stood down from direct combat, Iranian allies are engaged in the region, with Hezbollah confronting Israel in Lebanon and the Houthis advancing in Yemen.

Iran and its allies have significantly pressured oil exports from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states. The Houthis have disrupted ship traffic at the mouth of the Red Sea, while Iran has effectively limited tanker traffic at the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for 20 percent of the world’s oil exports before the start of the war. An attack by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq also temporarily knocked Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline out of service.

Security experts have debated exactly how much Iran directly influences the Houthis, a Shiite Islamist movement that evolved from a local insurgency into a powerful armed group controlling much of northern Yemen.

However, Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources have said the Houthis’ advance down Yemen’s Red Sea coast was carried out with direct guidance from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as “secondary sanctions.”

Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries including the UAE and Oman on Thursday in response to new US sanctions, the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in third countries that do business with Iran.

A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran’s isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea.

“We are living in an open-air prison,” a retired teacher in Tehran told Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.

news.title: Melania Trump Wows in Striking Look at Xi Jinping State Dinner
news.text:
Melania Trump put her fashion credentials on display as she joined President Donald Trump for the White House state dinner honoring Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The 56-year-old First Lady wore a striking monochrome look while welcoming Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the White House in Washington, DC, on Thursday evening.

For the black-tie occasion, Melania once again chose to forgo a traditional evening gown.

Instead, she selected a $2,300 Saint Laurent button-up blouse featuring oversized bow detailing around the neckline.

She teamed the blouse with $1,945 embossed high-waisted trousers and a $1,345 silk cummerbund, both from Dolce and Gabbana.

Her honey-colored hair was swept back from her face, while black pointed-toe Christian Louboutin heels and diamond stud earrings completed the ensemble.

Melania’s preference for wearing trousers to high-profile events has previously attracted intense scrutiny.

However, San Diego-based personal stylist and image consultant Cynthia Kennedy previously told Our News Outlet that the First Lady’s wardrobe choices convey a sense of independence and rebellion.

“She’s not doing what people expect. She’s not wearing safe, dull, traditional First Lady fashion,” Kennedy told Our News Outlet in April.

“She’s wearing what SHE wants, from her favorite designers – mostly European luxury brands like Dolce & Gabbana – and she’s making it clear that this job is something she’s doing on her own terms,” Kennedy added.

“What she’s doing may not necessarily be modern, but it is strategic.

“She’s showing that she’s on a completely different playing field and follows her own rules. She’s not interested in dressing for any role,” Kennedy said.

The Trumps hosted the Chinese delegation in the East Room, where both presidents delivered remarks during the state dinner.

Senior Cabinet officials and American business leaders were among the guests, including executives from Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Tesla and other major companies.

The lavish black-tie gathering was among the administration’s most star-studded events, creating a glamorous setting for easing long-standing geopolitical tensions with the Asian superpower.

Behind closed doors in the East Room, Melania’s office said it had personally overseen the evening’s elaborate arrangements. The space was transformed with red linens, Reagan-era vermeil and overflowing urns of crimson dahlias, reflecting an aesthetic the First Lady said “draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history.”

During the dinner, guests watched several performances, with military musicians and inauguration tenor Christopher Macchio providing a grand musical backdrop.

Inside the dining room, guests raised glasses of Schramsberg ‘Blanc De Noirs’ for a symbolic toast, reviving the historic 1972 ‘Toast to Peace’ between Richard Nixon and Premier Zhou Enlai in China.

White House chefs fused classic American ingredients with subtle Asian flavors across a lavish multi-course menu.

Xi arrived at Trump’s presidential airport, Joint Base Andrews, for a welcome ceremony on Wednesday evening. 

Trump personally greeted Xi at the airport ceremony despite the Chinese president not welcoming the US president at the airport during his trip to Beijing.

‘He decided to do it because they have a great relationship,’ First Lady Melania Trump said previously, ‘and we need to welcome them with the most respect.’

Earlier today, the Trumps welcomed Xi and his wife Madame Peng to the White House with an arrival ceremony on the State Floor before a military review in the Rose Garden and subsequent bilateral meetings.

But tonight’s state dinner is not the final event of the visit.

On Friday, the Trumps will host the first couple of China for tea at the White House before doing a tour of the National Archives, where they will view key US founding documents.

Xi and Madame Peng will then depart from Joint Base Andrews.

news.title: Iranian President Blames US for Middle East Conflict, Denies Nuclear Ambitions and Offers to Dilute Uranium
news.text:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Thursday that Tehran has no interest in developing a nuclear weapon, while insisting that Iran is prepared to open its nuclear program to international inspections. In an interview, he blamed Washington for the nearly seven-month conflict in the Middle East and accused the United States of shutting down diplomatic avenues.

During an exclusive appearance on Fox News’ “Special Report,” host Bret Baier asked Pezeshkian directly whether Iran wants a nuclear bomb. The Iranian president gave an unequivocal response.

“Absolutely not,” Pezeshkian said, pointing to repeated religious rulings from Iran’s late supreme leader declaring weapons of mass destruction forbidden and unlawful.

His comments came as Iran continues to face international scrutiny over its nuclear activities, including uranium enrichment at levels significantly higher than those generally associated with civilian energy production.

Those enrichment activities formed the central justification cited by President Donald Trump for launching Operation Epic Fury in February.

Pezeshkian suggested Thursday that Iran could consider reducing its enrichment levels and permitting independent verification as part of a broader effort to ease the standoff over its nuclear program.

“We have said we are willing to dilute” materials connected to weapons of mass destruction, Pezeshkian said, adding that Tehran is also prepared to allow international inspections.

The president also referred to a memorandum of understanding he signed with Trump in June. The agreement was intended to stop the fighting and create a pathway toward a wider deal between the United States and Iran, but ultimately failed.

Under the framework proposed by Washington, the two sides would have had 60 days to work toward a final agreement addressing Iran’s nuclear ambitions and the wider tensions between the countries.

“We have no problem with that. We reached an agreement with your president,” Pezeshkian said, referring to Trump, who signed the document.

“The agreement was signed, and we remain willing—and still want—to continue on that path,” he added.

Pezeshkian said the broader framework had already been settled and argued that Iran had not closed the Strait of Hormuz. He maintained that the waterway remained open without a legal basis or agreed framework for restricting it.

He accused the United States of initiating the attack and said Iran’s supreme leader, scientists, military commanders and government officials were killed as a result.

The Iranian president went on to fault Washington for the collapse of negotiations, while emphasizing that Tehran is still willing to pursue a diplomatic settlement.

“Instead of engaging in dialogue, America entered the conflict by bombing us first and closing off every possible route,” Pezeshkian said. “We are ready” to negotiate.

He argued that military pressure and blockades are not a legitimate way for a country to operate internationally, saying Iran would permit broad access to verify its activities but would not accept being pushed into submission or denied access.

Pezeshkian also placed responsibility for the wider war squarely on the United States.

“We are not seeking to kill Americans, and our actions demonstrate that,” he said. “America has sought to kill Iranians. What we know is that if we are attacked, we have to defend ourselves.”

Addressing U.S. military strikes — including Operation Outcast — and increasing secondary sanctions, Pezeshkian said Iran would continue resisting Washington’s campaign.

“This is something that has been the doing of the United States,” he said. “We will keep resisting. We will find ways, and the life of our country will continue. We will remain.

“Yes, we do have economic issues, certainly. But in order to remain, we will go through any hardship and endure.

“If America thinks that they can keep sanctioning us, we have nothing to do, nor do we consider any type of American elections. If the current American government, within international legal frameworks, wishes to reach an agreement, fine. If not, before the elections or after the elections, what difference does it make for us?”

Pezeshkian repeated that Iran does not want the war to continue, while blaming Israel for helping provoke the conflict and putting responsibility on Washington to bring it to an end.

“We will stand resolutely to defend ourselves. We never sought war. We do not seek war,” he said.

“I deeply believe that humans should not cause the death of another human. But with the instigations conducted by Israel, they have imposed this war on us.

“But we do not wish to continue. It’s America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not.”

The Iranian president also addressed reports that Iranian forces used Chinese satellite imagery to carry out a deadly strike on a U.S. base in Jordan. The attack resulted in the deaths of three U.S. service members.

When questioned about the reports, Pezeshkian denied direct knowledge.

“I’m specifically unaware of these purported images that you talk about,” Pezeshkian said. 

“Now, what do militaries do with one another between two countries? It is their own business within their own guidelines.”

news.title: Melania Trump 'beaming' as one change spotted by body language expert
news.text: Melania Trump gave a 'striking' appearance at the state dinner hosted for Xi Jinping on Thursday as a body language expert claimed the First Lady was 'beaming'. President Xi Jinping and his wife Madam Peng were greeted by Donald Trump and his wife Melania outside the White House before they joined the pair in heading in to the dinner. Body language expert Dr Lillian Glass told The Mirror : "There were many fascinating body-language signals during President Xi Jinping's state visit to the White House, but one of the most striking was First Lady Melania Trump . "Look at that smile! We have rarely seen Melania smile this broadly in public, with her teeth fully showing and her entire face appearing animated. "It is a radiant expression, and she looks genuinely engaged in the moment." The expert added Melania's visible happiness "comes during a remarkable week for her". Dr Glass said: "Just days ago at the United Nations, we saw another unusually bright smile when President Trump publicly acknowledged her work. "She smiled and waved as he praised her efforts. Now, at the White House state dinner, we see that radiance again." The expert, with over 30 years of experience, observed how this differs from her usual exposition. She said: "There appears to be a new confidence in Melania's public presentation. "She has spent this week stepping forward with her own initiatives and responsibilities, and she personally led preparations for this state dinner. "She is increasingly being seen not merely standing beside the President but undertaking highly visible work of her own." Dr Glass also noted that Melania made a "bold" outfit choice in a "black-and-white ensemble". She continued to add that Melania "is smiling broadly as she interacts with President Xi. She appears animated, engaged and comfortable." Dr Glass suggests that Melania appears to be "beaming" due to having "found a stronger public voice". The expert added: "Earlier this week at the U.N., I wrote that we were seeing a woman on a mission —a more serious Melania with greater vocal passion and determination as she promoted her work on the international stage. "Now we are seeing another side of that woman. She is beaming. "Perhaps the most interesting change is not simply that Melania is smiling more. It is that these smiles are appearing during a week in which she has assumed a particularly visible role of her own. "She has found a stronger public voice. Her work is receiving international attention. And when her husband publicly recognized those efforts at the U.N., we saw that brilliant smile emerge. "Now, beside him at the state dinner, we see it again." Dr Glass continued: "The serious, determined woman we saw pursuing her agenda at the United Nations is now standing on the White House red carpet positively radiant. "This may be the happiest and most visibly confident Melania we have seen in quite some time."
news.summary: Melania Trump was 'beaming' at the state dinner hosted as body language expert claims the First Lady appears to be 'the happiest and most visibly confident' we have seen her

news.title: Elon Musk, Tim Cook, Sam Altman Among Guests At Trump's State Dinner For Xi
news.text: US President Donald Trump hosted Chinese leader Xi Jinping for a lavish state dinner at the White House on Thursday, after a day of pomp and ceremony that masked deep tensions between the rival superpowers.Numerous US tech titans attended the banquet, including Tesla's Elon Musk, Apple's Tim Cook, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Sam Altman of OpenAI, underscoring that trade and artificial intelligence were high on the agenda for Xi's visit.Protesters gathered outside the White House as Trump and his wife Melania welcomed Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan for dinner, chanting slogans including "Xi Jinping is not welcome" and "Free Hong Kong," AFP reporters witnessed.Earlier in the day, Trump proclaimed that he and Xi had made "tremendous strides" as he laid on pageantry including a military parade, a flyover and a tour of his new White House helipad.Elon Musk attends a state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump. Photo Credit: Reuters"President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure," Trump said at the dinner.But Xi took a more restrained tone, calling for China and the United States to "coexist in peace" even as he laid down Beijing's red lines on AI, Taiwan and the Iran war.He continued the theme in his dinner remarks, saying: "China and the United States must act as responsible major countries."Bald eagle statueTrump presented Xi with a gift of a custom-made statue of a bald eagle -- the national symbol of the United States. Guests dined on yellow squash veloute, sesame crusted sea bass, and vanilla cremeux with White House honey ice cream.The 80-year-old US president invited guests to tour the building site of his new $400 million ballroom after the dinner, saying: "In honor of you, you'll be the first people to step foot on that."While business was on the menu at the state dinner, expectations of any major breakthroughs from Xi's visit are low.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang attend a state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump. Photo Credit: ReutersOne minor success -- the extension of a trade truce by two months until January -- was less than the two years that the Chinese had been hoping for.Instead, the visit was more about spectacle than substance, with the pomp helping to smooth over the tensions that divide the world's two top economies.A formal welcome on the White House South Lawn launched Thursday's events, before Trump and Xi inspected a military parade on the newly paved-over Rose Garden. American military jets -- including a B-2 bomber of the type that bombed Iranian nuclear facilities last year -- then staged a flyover as US and Chinese flags flew over the West Wing.As they began talks in the Oval Office, Trump joked that the Chinese had the friendliest press corps.His comment came days after he barred outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House -- although they returned on Thursday after a court order.'Great meeting' Trump later walked Xi out to see the new helipad he has built at the White House, and took the Chinese leader aboard his Marine One helicopter."We had a great meeting," Trump said, as the pair ignored questions on subjects including Iran, Taiwan, fentanyl trafficking and jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai.But Xi's comments were often pointed. In his arrival remarks he said the two countries must ensure there is "no conflict and no confrontation" and said that AI must remain "always under human control."Trump has in contrast played down warnings that AI could threaten humanity.Later in the Oval, Xi urged Trump to show "prudence" and oppose independence for the flashpoint of Taiwan, the self-governing island that Beijing claims.The Chinese leader -- whose country has reportedly shared intelligence with Tehran -- also urged Trump to end the Iran war "through negotiation as soon as possible." Xi's visit wraps up on Friday as the presidential couples pay a visit to the US National Archives, home to the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary this year.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

news.title: Small bites from the UN: Defiance, fiery speeches and a cold building
news.text:
Competing speeches from Benjamin Netanyahu and Mahmoud Abbas commanded attention at the United Nations on Thursday, even though the Palestinian leader wasn't there in person: The United States denied him a visa.

Plenty of other stories unfolded Thursday that affect all parts of the world, as presidents and leaders and kings stand up, one after another, to speak to the UN General Assembly meetings. Here are a few:

A promise to stay home

Thursday marked Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella's first chance to address the gathering of world leaders.

He passed it up.

De la Espriella, who took office last month, promised on the campaign trail that if he won, he would forgo foreign trips so he could focus on the country's internal problems, especially urban crime and the violence caused by illegal armed groups.

So on Thursday, Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo took the rostrum to deliver a speech in his president's stead. He said it was the president's own words that he would present.

The speech began by hailing Colombia's resilience in the wake of a powerful earthquake that killed at least 289 people last month.

On topics including security, economic growth, the leaders are trying to change the course of “a country that is well aware of its difficulties but also of its enormous potential.”

“Believe in Colombia,” De la Espriella said, via Restrepo. “I don't promise you a perfect country, but I assure you that I am working tirelessly to build a nation that is safer, more prosperous and with more opportunities for its people.”

Long live the fatherland, damn it!'

Only 10 months into his presidency, Bolivia's Rodrigo Paz Pereira has faced turmoil at home. Many of his originally appointed ministers are gone after political ruptures, corruption scandals and street protests. His efforts to shore up Bolivia's scarce fuel supplies backfired when contaminated gasoline damaged more than 10,000 vehicles. The seat of his government came under siege for almost eight weeks as demanded his resignation.

But on Thursday, Paz struck a defiant tone. He said the economy is improving, they are successfully managing fuel shortages, and people are looking to the future.

Socialism “does not put food on the table” he said. Instead, he said, in electing him, Bolivia “decided to engage in a change and a transformation and to not turn back to the past.”

He ended his speech with might be the quote of the assembly so far: “Long live the fatherland, damn it! Long live Bolivia.”

Referencing Trump's annihilate' comment on Israel

Ghana President John Dramani Mahama seemed to reference Donald Trump's speech on Tuesday when the US president suggested he might “annihilate” Iran.

Said Mahama: “No human civilisation deserves to be annihilated, and certainly not a member of the United Nations."

He touted recognition of a resolution to recognise the crimes of transatlantic slave trade, thanking 123 nations that voted to affirm it. Ghana, formerly the Gold Coast, was a key slave trafficking port in the 1600s and 1700s.

“No race is superior. No nation is inferior. No child's life is worth less because of the language they speak, the faith they profess, the colour of their skin or the land of their birth,” he said. “This is the unyielding moral foundation upon which the United Nations must stand.”

Fiery speakers brought the heat, but the building itself was cold

As a cost-saving measure, UN Secretary-General kept the temperature in the sprawling UN headquarters complex warmer than some staffers would have liked in the summer heat.

But with fall just arriving and temperatures in New York significantly lower on Thursday, there were complaints during a press conference on the state of global education that the press briefing room felt like an icebox. One correspondent — yes, ours — went to get a shawl. Others closed their jackets. Everyone left with cold hands.

UN deputy spokesman Farhan Haq, who moderated an event in the room laughed and said of its very chilly temperature: “It's whatever the weather is like outside – and more.”

Paraguay stands with Taiwan

During his speech to the UN General Assembly, Paraguayan President Santiago Peña spoke about the conflict in the Indo-Pacific region and reiterated his country's support for the island of Taiwan.

“Paraguay stands, and I say this loud and clear, with Taiwan,” he said.

Paraguay is the only country in South America to recognise Taiwan and one of just 12 worldwide. Beijing considers Taiwan its own territory and has ramped up a campaign over the past few years to lure away Taiwan's diplomatic allies, in addition to increasing military pressure around the island.

Taiwan is the global hub of microchip manufacturing and, according to Peña, conflicts in the region impact the microchips that “drive industry, defence, and artificial intelligence.”

“What happens there is not merely a regional matter ... It affects Japan, all of East and Southeast Asia, and, above all, it affects the global economy,” he said. “Anyone who pretends that this is far away or too distant simply has not understood the 21st century.”

Published on September 25, 2026
news.summary: World leaders used the UN General Assembly to address security, economic challenges, national priorities and growing geopolitical tensions across regions

news.title: Trump lays out the pomp for Xi but says little about the significant tensions in US-China relations
news.text: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met for high stakes talks on Thursday at an urgent moment for the US-China relationship, with the world’s preeminent powers divided on the war in Iran and still grappling to find common ground on trade and how to best navigate the jarring advances of artificial intelligence.With their countries in a generational contest for economic and technological dominance, the two appear to be betting that a combination of personal rapport and mutual interest can prevent the competition from boiling over into open conflict.“From the time of my first election in 2016, President Xi and I have forged a friendship, a truly great friendship, actually, built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people,” Trump said as he welcomed Xi to the White House for a pomp-filled state visit.Xi was more pointed than Trump, saying Chinese and American interests are “deeply intertwined” and that the “competition should be a healthy one and should be kept within bounds.”He also reiterated his warning that the U.S. and China must avoid the “ Thucydides trap,” referring to the idea that when a rising power threatens to displace an established one, the result is often war. Xi offered a similar warning when Trump visited Beijing in May.“It should be a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses,” Xi added.China has resisted the Trump administration's urgings — and economic threats — to use its considerable leverage to prod Iran to agree to U.S. terms to end the nearly seven-month war. Xi wants to see Trump permanently halt arms sales to Taiwan and loosen export restrictions on cutting-edge advanced chips. The two sides on Wednesday agreed to extend by two months a one-year trade truce that was set to expire Nov. 10 as they work to find a more durable agreement.Xi presses Trump on TaiwanDuring their private conversation on Thursday, Xi told Trump he hopes the U.S. can adhere to opposing Taiwan independence and urged him to “prudently handle the Taiwan issue,” according to the Chinese state media outlet Xinhua. The White House did not immediately release any readout of the talks and Trump, who frequently offers his own take of his interactions with foreign leaders on his social media platform, has yet to weigh in on the substance of his conversations with Xi.Trump, who is in the midst of a legal fight after trying to bar CNN, MSNOW, and Politico from the White House, did complain that TV networks “refused to cover one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years.” The White House’s five-network television pool rotation refused to cover Trump’s events in response to the action against CNN.China has made clear it views Taiwan as the most sensitive issue in the U.S.-China relationship. Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and vows to annex the island by force if necessary. The United States is obligated by law to provide Taiwan with sufficient hardware to deter any armed attack from the mainland. The U.S. has said it opposes any unilateral changes to the status quo by either side.China has repeatedly pressed Washington to permanently halt the arms sales, including when Trump and Xi met in Beijing in May.After that meeting, Trump said he was holding off on final approval for a record $14 billion arms package that was in the pipeline. He also described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” with China.Xi says China and US should make sure AI is ‘always under human control’Trump said in a social media post earlier Thursday that artificial intelligence — “superintelligence” as he is trying to rebrand it — was high on the agenda. The president has been dismissive of calls for greater regulation amid growing global anxiety that the technology will kill jobs or potentially even wipe out humanity.“I want to leave it exactly where it is,” Trump wrote. “That is China’s position also.”But Xi, in his opening comments, said that the two countries had “the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people.”The two countries’ finance ministers met earlier this week, with the U.S. proposing a new “notification mechanism” for AI incidents between the two nations.Trump rolls out the red carpet for XiTrump had made clear he wanted to impress Xi with the visit. The Republican president made sure construction of a new helicopter landing pad on the White House's South Lawn was completed before the visit and he met Xi and his wife on Wednesday evening when they flew into Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.The White House also arranged an elaborate military review, which the leaders and their spouses observed before the Oval Office talks.After about 90 minutes of talks, the leaders stepped out to the South Lawn so Trump could show off the new White House helipad and give Xi a tour of Marine One, the presidential helicopter. Trump and Xi also appeared to peer at the ballroom construction site from afar. Xi left the White House shortly after the quick tour and returned in the evening for the state dinner.No Chinese CEOs at state dinnerTech titans, including Amazon's Jeff Bezos, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and Tesla and SpaceX's Elon Musk, were among the 130 guests invited to the black-tie dinner, but Chinese CEOs were conspicuously absent.U.S. and Chinese planners did discuss including several executives from some notable Chinese companies, according to a person familiar with the planning for the state visit who was not authorized to comment publicly.One obstacle that came up during the negotiations for the state visits was that the U.S. side was slow to propose protocols and clarify the roles the Chinese CEOs would have during the state visit, the person said. The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the absence of Chinese business leaders.While Trump has offered plenty of glitz, some China analysts observed that the talks seemed light on substance.Danny Russel, a former senior State Department official who served in former President Barack Obama's administration, observed that the two leaders spent more time in social and ceremonial events than in formal talks about the core issues facing the two nations.“What we’re seeing isn’t diplomacy so much as ‘diplotainment,’ which won’t do much to solve the serious problems in the US-China relationship,” said Russel, who is now a distinguished fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute..Xi urges US and Iran to return to interim agreementThe two sides discussed the ongoing conflict in Iran, according to Chinese state broadcaster China Central Television.Trump has argued to little effect that China, which is far more dependent on Gulf oil than the U.S., has plenty of incentive to use its sway with Tehran to help force an end to the conflict.But Trump's war of choice has unnerved Beijing, with the government condemning the U.S. and Israeli military action and Xi previously expressing concerns that the conflict signaled a return to what he called the “law of the jungle.” The U.S. administration has warned China, Tehran's biggest trading partner, not to aid Iran’s military effort.Xi, during Thursday's talks, said China supports the U.S. and Iran returning to a short-lived interim deal from the summer to wind down the war, according to CCTV. That agreement broke down soon after it was signed in June as the countries traded renewed fire over control of the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for energy shipments.

CARACAS, Venezuela (AFP)—Hundreds of protesters demanded the return of exiled opposition figure and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado to Venezuela, AFP observed at a demonstration in Caracas on Thursday.

“Maria Corina, come, we’re waiting for you!” the crowd chanted, marching under an enormous Venezuelan flag.

Machado was blocked from entering the country on Tuesday after yet another attempt to return home, sources from her political party told AFP.

That same day, Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez met with US President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Protester Douglas Mata, 65, questioned why Machado had been prevented from coming home.

“It’s not possible that they receive Delcy Rodriguez like a queen in the United States, yet they won’t let Maria Corina enter her own country,” he said.

Rodriguez took over from President Nicolas Maduro after his ouster by US forces in January, and has effectively governed under Washington’s thumb since then.

The White House denies allegations that Trump has vetoed Machado’s return to Venezuela.

The opposition figure came out of hiding in December, when she traveled to Norway to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

After a brief stint in the United States, she settled in Panama City, where she now lives in exile.

news.title: Netanyahu calls Mamdani ‘antisemitic mayor’ in UN speech, accuses him of spreading lies
news.text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Mayor Zohran Mamdani of endangering Jewish New Yorkers with his criticism of Israel’s military actions in Gaza, saying during a speech at the United Nations on Thursday that the mayor has spread lies about Israel.

Calling Mamdani “the antisemitic mayor of New York,” Netanyahu spent part of his time speaking to the United Nations General Assembly to assail the man who threatened to have him arrested if he came to the city.

“Mr Mamdani, since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York. They talk to me, they tell me this isn’t the city we remember, it changed so quickly,’” Netanyahu said.

It’s the latest in a back-and-forth between the Netanyahu and New York City’s first Muslim mayor, who has long been a vocal critic of Israel’s military actions in Gaza and has called Netanyahu a “war criminal” who is “the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people.” Mamdani has said that his criticism of Israel and advocacy for Palestinian rights don’t amount to antisemitism.

Trump praised for support of Israel

The mayor met with US President Donald Trump this week in New York. Netanyahu, during his speech Thursday, praised the president for his support of Israel, saying “we’ve had no greater partner than President Trump.”

Mamdani’s office did not immediately comment on Netanyahu’s speech.

Mamdani’s stance on Netanyahu arrest

During his mayoral campaign last year, Mamdani said he would direct police in New York to execute an arrest warrant against Netanyahu issued by the International Criminal Court, but has more recently acknowledged the city does not have the authority to take him into custody.

The mayor has since encouraged the federal government to arrest Netanyahu, though Trump has said the prime minister will not be arrested.

“Mr Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can’t silence me and you can’t silence the truth,” Netanyahu said in his speech.

Published on September 25, 2026
news.summary: The Israeli prime minister used his UN address to directly confront New York’s mayor over his criticism of Israel’s Gaza actions

news.title: Justice Jackson says Supreme Court intervenes too quickly on Trump's side
news.text:
WASHINGTON − Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson continued her ongoing criticism of how her colleagues are handling emergency appeals, telling an audience on Sept. 24 that requests for immediate intervention can’t become a “special avenue that certain privileged litigants can use selectively.”

“As one of my colleagues recently suggested in an opinion,” Jackson said during remarks at the University of the District of Columbia law school, “some frequent emergency docket filers have the court on speed dial.”

Although Jackson never mentioned the Trump administration, she was referring to Justice Sonia Sotomayor’s dissent last year when the conservative court backed the administration in a dispute with a federal judge over the administration’s attempt to deport eight migrants to South Sudan.

In her own opinions, Jackson − one of the three liberal justices − has complained that the court is showing preferential treatment for the government, along with a willingness to undercut lower court judges.

She did so last year when the court allowed the administration to block $783 million in grants for health research.

“This is Calvinball jurisprudence with a twist,” Jackson wrote, referring to a made-up game in the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes. “Calvinball has only one rule: There are no fixed rules. We seem to have two: that one, and this Administration always wins.”

More: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson can throw a punch. Literally.

The rulings she referenced came on emergency requests from the administration to let a controversial policy move forward while it’s being challenged in court.

When major policies of President Donald Trump have come before the justices for a final ruling, the court permanently shut down his attempts to use emergency powers to impose tariffs and to rewrite citizenship rules. 

But a majority has more often than not sided with the president on the interim decisions about Trump’s policies that are decided without a full record or oral arguments.

Jackson said the Supreme Court didn’t use to get involved as often in the early stages of the litigation. Instead, the justices “waited humbly until the facts were established and the lower courts had fully and fairly assessed the law.”

“It was only in exigent circumstances, actual emergencies, that the justices felt the need to intervene in pending cases,” she said. “I think the justices understood that very little good comes from taking an institution that is supposed to be operating outside of the political realm and routinely steering it into the fray.”

But in recent years, Jackson said, the court “has been noticeably less restrained, especially with respect to pending cases that involve controversial matters.”

More: A clock, a mural, a petition: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson's chambers tell her story

In those cases, Jackson said, anyone seeking the court’s early help should have to show that something harmful is about to happen “in the real world” without intervention.

If they can do that, then the justices should issue a ruling based on which side will experience the greater harm.

“We have an appellate review process with an equitable emergency exception that can sometimes warrant the Supreme Court’s early intervention, but only when exigent circumstances require it,” she said. “I feel strongly that we should be sticking to that history and tradition.”

news.title: 'One of the Easiest Decisions': Benjamin Netanyahu on Israel’s Attack on Iran at UN (Video)
news.text:
Delegates Walk Out During Netanyahu's UN Speech

Netanyahu's address was marked by a significant walkout. Dozens of delegates left the chamber as he began speaking, in a visible protest against Israel's policies and military actions. Netanyahu responded by challenging those who remained in the hall to leave as well, accusing the departing delegates of failing to confront what he described as threats posed by Iran. The walkout highlighted the deep divisions surrounding Israel's conduct of the war in Gaza and its military confrontation with Iran. Netanyahu Warns Hamas over Gaza Launches as Group Accuses Israel of Escalation.

Netanyahu Rejects Gaza Genocide Allegations

The Israeli prime minister also used his UN address to reject allegations that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza. Netanyahu described the accusations as “the biggest lie of the century” and defended Israel's military campaign against Hamas. Israel has repeatedly rejected genocide allegations and says its operations are directed at Hamas rather than the Palestinian population.

The Gaza war began after the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel, which killed about 1,200 people and resulted in 251 people being taken hostage, according to Israeli figures cited by Reuters. Israel subsequently launched its military campaign in Gaza.

Netanyahu Takes Aim at New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani

Netanyahu also directly criticised New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has been outspoken in his opposition to Israel's actions in Gaza. The Israeli prime minister accused Mamdani of supporting Hamas and criticised his descriptions of Israel's military conduct. Mamdani has rejected the accusation of supporting Hamas and has criticised Netanyahu's policies. The UN appearance was Netanyahu's first visit to New York since Mamdani became mayor in January, adding another layer to the political tensions surrounding the speech.

Iran Conflict Remains Central to UN Debate

Netanyahu's remarks came as the Iran conflict remained one of the central issues at this year's UN General Assembly. US President Donald Trump had also used his UN address to defend the US decision to launch military action against Iran while maintaining that negotiations could still produce a settlement.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said Tehran does not seek nuclear weapons but would not accept restrictions on what it describes as its peaceful nuclear programme. Against that backdrop, Netanyahu presented Israel's attack on Iran's nuclear facilities as a necessary security measure and said Israel would continue to defend itself against threats from Iran and its regional allies.

Netanyahu Says Israel Will Continue Fighting

Toward the end of his address, Netanyahu maintained that Israel would continue its military campaign despite international criticism. His speech brought together several of Israel's key arguments over the Iran conflict, Gaza war and confrontation with Hamas and Hezbollah, while also directly addressing some of Israel's most prominent international critics. The address reflected the widening diplomatic divisions over the Middle East conflicts as world leaders gathered in New York for the 81st UN General Assembly.
news.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Israel’s military action against Iran during his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, saying the decision to attack Iranian nuclear facilities was “one of the easiest decisions” he had made as prime minister.

news.title: Trump Embarrassed by Protesters Interrupting His Dictator Suck-Up Session
news.text:
Anti-China protesters put a damper on President Donald Trump’s wooing of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Dozens of protesters made their voices heard outside the White House North Portico on Thursday evening ahead of Trump’s star-studded state dinner with Xi.

One protester could even be heard yelling what sounded like, “F--- you, Melania” as the two leaders and their wives entered the White House.

Among the non-governmental personnel present at Trump’s fawning dinner were tech billionaires Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos; Fox News personalities Jesse Watters, Bret Baier, and Laura Ingraham; and CEOs David Ellison, Darren Woods, and David Solomon.

Trump’s Cabinet officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche, were on the guest list, as were Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett, Brett Kavanaugh, and John Roberts.

Trump, 80, rolled out the red carpet for Xi—literally—on Wednesday, as the Chinese Communist Party leader was welcomed onto U.S. soil for the first time since November 2023.

While China’s paramount leader remained steadfast in his awareness of the significance of their meeting, Trump seemed more interested in the spectacle, bragging to Xi about his new helipad and his Wall of Fame mocking former President Joe Biden.

Xi stressed for the second time in four months that China and the U.S. need to avoid the “Thucydides trap”—a historical theory that warns tensions between a rising superpower and an established one can quickly spiral into war. 

The Chinese president called for the two nations to “coexist in peace” and asked that U.S. competition be “kept within bounds.”

Trump, however, focused more on his relationship with Xi, saying his Chinese counterpart was a “truly great friend” and that the day they spent together was “magnificent.”

In a head-scratching move, Trump once again denied CNN, MS NOW, and Politico’s access to the state dinner’s arrivals without warning, even after reinstating their access to the White House earlier in the day in compliance with a federal judge’s ruling.

CNN reporter Kristen Holmes explained the confusing development as Trump and Xi met on the North Portico.

“We received an email from the White House asking who would be attending. We responded that… we would only be sending editorial. That is what the agreement has been,” she said, referencing the TV networks not sending a pool until the ban was listed.
news.summary:

Dozens of protesters made their voices heard outside the White House North Portico on Thursday evening ahead of Trump’s star-studded state dinner with Xi.

As the two world leaders posed for photos outside before the dinner, protesters could be heard chanting “Free Hong Kong” and “Free Tibet,” among other anti-China sentiments, even amid the sounds of the U.S. Marine Band.

news.title: Tom Sandoval catches strays as ‘Special Forces’ instructor compares him to George Santos: ‘They don’t hold themselves accountable’
news.text:
Jovon “Q” Quarles, a member of the directing staff on Fox’s “Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test,” said disgraced New York representative George Santos reminded him of “Vanderpump Rules” alum Tom Sandoval.

The former NAVY SEAL spoke exclusively to Page Six’s “Virtual Reali-Tea” about Santos — who served prison time after being convicted of federal wire fraud and aggravated identity theft — and his stint on the Fox show’s fifth season.

“He reminds me of Tom Sandoval, where, ‘Nothing I’ve done was wrong. Nothing I did was wrong,’ and then [they] point the finger at the other person and say that what [that person] did was wrong,” Quarles told us. 

“They don’t hold themselves accountable.”

Sandoval infamously competed on the show’s second season shortly after his months-long affair with Rachel “Raquel” Leviss was exposed in 2023, ending his nine-year relationship with Ariana Madix.

Quarles, who served 15 years as a NAVY SEAL, has been a part of the “Special Forces” directing staff since Season 2. He, along with three other former military operatives, run the rigorous course that a new group of celebrities and athletes attempt to complete each season.

Quarles told us that he was aware of Santos’ criminal history, which included embezzling funds from campaign donors to pay for personal luxuries, including Botox and spa days, as well as making false claims about his education, employment history and heritage.

Santos was sentenced to more than seven years in prison, but only served three months before President Donald Trump commuted his sentence and he was released.

“There was no bit of me that was going to be light with him at all,” Quarles said. “I wanted to make sure he understood what we deal with, as men and women in the Special Forces, and what it’s like.”

As someone who has been deployed multiple times with the military, Quarles said he took Santos’ history of “fraud” and “scandals” to heart, noting that elected politicians are supposed to tell the “truth” and have the “backs” of their military personnel. 

“We’re supposed to trust you?” Quarles — who expressed his hope to see more politicians try their hands at future seasons — wondered. “And then you send us out here to go to war to die for stuff that you are lying about for the most part.”

“I took it personally, so I really wanted to challenge him and really give him a taste of what it’s like to understand that, ‘Hey, you now don’t have any control.'”

While the DS did not take it easy on Santos, Quarles did get a good laugh out of watching the convicted fraudster’s many failed attempts at pulling himself out of the lake water and onto the dock in the Season 5 premiere episode.

“Seeing Santos flop back in was like seeing a dead sea lion just kind of roll over and fall back [into] the water,” Quarles chuckled. “It was the funniest thing.”

“Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test” airs on Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET on Fox, with new episodes available to stream the next day on Hulu.

news.title: Donald Trump sparks health fears as he 'nods off' during key Xi Jinping speech
news.text: US President Donald Trump triggered fresh health concerns as he welcomed Xi Jinping at a state dinner on Thursday. Trump greeted the Chinese President and his wife Madam Peng outside the White House with his wife Melania by his side, with focus once more turning to the state of his hands. American journalist Aaron Rupar remarked on his physical condition via X. Posting photographs, he observed how discoloured the president's hand appeared before commenting: "Yikes: Trump's hands - both of them - are looking rough tonight." Detailed images of the leader's hands reveal them as discoloured and apparently caked in makeup. The right hand particularly seems to be coated from wrist to fingertips in concealing cosmetics, while only a minor area of skin appears covered on his left hand. Trump's wellbeing remains under the microscope throughout his second presidency, including regarding bruising visible on his hands and puffiness around his ankles. Nevertheless, a doctor has declared him to be in "excellent health". Additional worries emerged when the president addressed attendees inside the White House during the state dinner. The US president welcomed visitors, discussing the "long history" between China and the US before presenting Xi with a bald eagle statue. "The bald eagle is a national symbol of the United States and an embodiment of the free and soaring spirit of America," Trump declared. "We hope it'll find a nice place, a wonderful place in Beijing." Given the guest list and Xi's limited English, Trump would pause after delivering several portions of his speech to allow an interpreter to read aloud a translated version. During these intervals, Trump remained at the lectern somewhat uncomfortably, frequently seeming to shut his eyes. This marks another instance where the president has been observed closing his eyes during a significant event. It has been documented on multiple occasions that the 80 year old 'dozes off' while in meetings. When the Express enquired about the President's wellbeing in June, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle responded: "President Trump's sharpness, unmatched energy, and historic accessibility stand in stark contrast to what we saw during the last administration when Democrats and the legacy media intentionally covered up Joe Biden 's serious mental and physical decline from the American people. "President Trump is the sharpest and most accessible President in American history who is working nonstop to solve problems and deliver on his promises." The health worries follow his earlier encounter with Xi, which also raised alarm when he seemed to sway sideways while walking down the red carpet before the Chinese leader's entrance.
news.summary: Donald Trump's hands appeared discoloured and covered in make-up as he greeted Xi Jinping at a White House state dinner. He also appeared to close his eyes during interpreter pauses in his speech

news.title: Xi Jinping Invites 1,00,000 Young Americans to China; Know the Reason
news.text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping announced on Thursday, September 24, that one lakh young Americans will be invited to visit China for educational exchanges and study programs over the next five years. Speaking at the White House alongside US President Donald Trump, Xi highlighted historical ties and people-to-people connections as foundational pillars for stabilising bilateral relations between the two global powers.

People-to-People Exchanges and Historical Ties

The newly announced initiative builds upon a previous program launched in 2023, which successfully brought 50,000 young Americans to China for similar exchanges ahead of its projected timeline, reports PTI. “The hope of China-US relationship lies in our people, and its future lies with the young. I am glad to announce an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years,” Xi said. During his remarks, the Chinese leader invoked the shared history of World War II, noting that forces from both nations fought side-by-side against fascist aggression. “Chinese people have never forgotten that part of history, nor have the American people,” Xi noted. He added, “Achieving the Great Rejuvenation of the Chinese Nation and making America great again can go hand in hand. Let us meet the people’s expectations and show our historical initiative. Let us keep advancing the cause of friendship between our two peoples, and work together to build a better world.”

Joint Commitments and Common Interests

President Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese delegation and pointed to shared historical milestones, referencing American involvement during World War II and the historic efforts of the "Flying Tigers" pilot group. Trump emphasised that bilateral cooperation spans across security, technology, and emerging fields like superintelligence, noting that collaborative leadership can secure decades of mutual peace and prosperity.

“Pursuit of those common interests has connected our people across the vast oceans of big, tremendous distances and many differences, and even made us allies in World War II,” Trump said. Recalling historical lexicon born from cross-cultural cooperation, Trump remarked, “Look at the greatness that we had together fighting in World War II. Brave American pilots volunteered to come to China and fight for the very survival of the legendary country, that legendary Flying Tigers group. “And it was the United States Marines’ encounter with Chinese people that inspired the Marines to adopt a Chinese phrase they still use today, ‘Gung Ho,’” Trump added. “The Marines use it as an expression of great enthusiasm, but in Chinese it literally means working together.”

news.title: 'Let's Nurture Beautiful Flowers Of Friendship': Xi, Trump Call For Stronger Ties At White House State Dinner
news.text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump called for stronger ties between Beijing and Washington during a White House state dinner on Thursday, with Xi saying their meeting had produced a common understanding on several issues and Trump stressing the importance of maintaining close relations despite differences between the two countries.
Welcoming Xi and First Lady Peng Liyuan to the White House, Trump said the relationship between the two countries had strengthened despite differences in their political systems.
“As the leaders of our two nations, President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better...Together, we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations,” Trump said.
Xi Calls For ‘New Chapter’ In Ties
Addressing the dinner, Xi thanked Trump and First Lady Melania Trump for their hospitality and said the arrangements made for his visit reflected careful attention to detail.
“Thank you, Mr. President and Mrs. Trump, for extending to my wife and me your gracious hospitality and thoughtful arrangements. You and Mrs. Trump have made many special arrangements for our visit, all prepared with meticulous care and consideration in every detail. You make us feel truly at home,” Xi said.
The Chinese President also said his meeting with Trump involved “sincere and in-depth exchanges” and resulted in a common understanding on several issues.
“Today, President Trump and I had sincere and in-depth exchanges and reached a common understanding on many issues. This has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and provided new strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations,” he said.
Xi recalled Trump's visit to China in May, saying the two leaders had agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship based on strategic stability.
“In May this year, President Trump paid a successful visit to China at my invitation. We agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. During the visit, President Trump warmly invited me to visit the United States, and I have come as promised,” Xi said.
He noted that the Chinese and American presidents had exchanged state visits in less than six months, describing the development as a significant moment in bilateral engagement.

“Like a river that never stops flowing, history never stands still. The friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise. Let us join hands and move forward side by side. Trump Recalls Beijing Visit

“This is a great honour. President Xi, Madam Peng and members of the Chinese delegation, Melania and I are delighted to welcome you once again to the White House. You are truly outstanding, amazing people,” Trump said.

“The bald eagle is a national symbol of the United States and an embodiment of the free and soaring spirit of America,” Trump said.
“We hope it'll find a nice place, a wonderful place in Beijing,” he added.

news.title: Netanyahu at UN: ‘Gaza genocide allegations are the biggest lie of the century’
news.text:
Allegations of Israeli genocide in Gaza are not only false but “the biggest lie of the century,” Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told world leaders Thursday in a defiant speech that asserted his nation's right to wage war against Iran — and was not heard by scores of delegates who trooped out before he started speaking.

Netanyahu, his voice rising in emphasis, said attacking Iran “was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make” and denounced as “moral cowards” a mass of delegates who walked out of the UN General Assembly when he took the podium to speak.

“In defending itself, Israel is also also defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall,” Netanyahu said. “In fact, I want you to know that many of their leaders even thank us privately for taking out Iran's nukes.”

When Netanyahu walked to the rostrum, a mix of cheers, boos and mass walkouts erupted. Scores of delegates marched out and a majority of visible seats sat empty afterward. “Order in the hall, please,” General Assembly President Khalilur Rahman said repeatedly.

“If there are any other moral cowards who have not yet left the hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said.

His remarks — which at times sounded like a stump speech as Israel gears up for elections — came after a week filled with speeches by world leaders accusing Israel of genocide and war crimes in Gaza.''

Palestinians had called for a mass walkout

The Palestinian Mission to the UN said in a message to many of the 193 UN member nations to bring as many staff as possible to the assembly hall and “collectively walk out of the assembly” once the Israeli prime minister is announced.

“This will send a clear message to Netanyahu and his government that no one is willing to aid, abet, or be complicit in its genocide and war crimes and illegal occupation, which all peace-loving states and peoples demand must come to an end,” the message said.

Israel rejects allegations that it committed genocide and war crimes and is illegally occupying Palestinian territory. All Israeli settlements are illegal under international law, but the Israeli government insists they are legal.

Netanyahu, who is prone to using visual aids during his General Assembly speeches, at one point held up a pager while reminding the audience of September 17, 2024, when Israel remotely detonatedthousands of pagers that had been distributed to the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon. The pager attack wounded more than 3,000 people and killed 12, including two children.

He reminded the assembly of the scale of the Oct. 7, 2023, attack in which Hamas militants killed about 1,200 people. “This is equal to 40,000 innocent Americans slaughtered in less than 24 hours,” he said, or 16 times the death count on the 9/11 attacks that left nearly 3,000 people dead in New York.

Netanyahu thanked US President Donald Trump for taking decisive action against Iran, and he insisted Israel would prevail: “We will continue to win because we have no other choice.”

Netanyahu followed the Palestinian president's remote speech

Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas also addressed the UN General Assembly earlier Thursday, delivering prerecorded remarks from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas to attend the gathering for the second year in a row.

The 90-year-old leader's popularity at home and relevance abroad have both waned. But in his remarks, Abbas made clear he did not intend to quietly accept being sidelined.

“We will not leave our homeland. We will not accept displacement. And we will not allow anyone to decide our future on our behalf,” Abbas said.

Though world leaders have repeatedly invoked the plight of Palestinians in speeches throughout the week, Abbas urged the international community to take more tangible action against Israel.

"How long will some countries continue to remain silent about Israel, or continue supplying it with weapons that it uses against our people? The world has witnessed the enormous cost in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank," Abbas said. “What, then, is the international community waiting for before it acts to protect the Palestinian people?”

Netanyahu is in the city of a mayor who wants him arrested

In past years, Netanyahu has used his General Assembly speech to both denounce the United Nations as biased and make Israel's case to world leaders. His address — scheduled for prime time in Israel — is the cornerstone of an abbreviated trip to the United States unfolding under the shadow of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani calling him a “war criminal” and pushing for his arrest.

Mamdani has acknowledged that New York does not have the authority to execute an International Criminal Court warrant but urged federal authorities to do so.

Israel has grown increasingly isolated throughout the war in Gaza. The war began on Oct. 7, 2023, when Hamas-led militants attacked Israel, killing around 1,200 people and kidnapping 251. At least 73,922 Palestinians have been killed in Israel's subsequent offensive, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-run government whose numbers are generally considered reliable by the international community.

A ceasefire agreed to by Israel and Hamas last October halted the heaviest of the fighting and led to the release of the remaining hostages yet further steps have since stalled. Israel maintains control of most of Gaza and continues to carry out airstrikes on Palestinians near military-held zones. Hamas not disarmed or relinquished power and there has been no progress toward reconstruction in the mostly destroyed territory.

Netanyahu has said no Palestinian state will be established while he is Israel's leader and has argued that the Palestinian Authority is not a partner for peace.

Netanyahu dismissed incidents of Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank as a “handful of young juvenile delinquents” throwing stones, chopping down olive trees and lighting fires.

“I can't stand that. I won't stand for vigilantism,” the prime minister said before accusing foreign leaders and the international press of distorting the scale of violence in the West Bank.

Netanyahu's government is dominated by settlers and their allies, including the Cabinet minister who oversees the police. There have been few arrests of settlers involved in attacks on Palestinians.

Israel captured the West Bank and east Jerusalem in the 1967 war, and the Palestinians want both as part of their future state. The Palestinians and much of the international community view the settlements as illegal and as an obstacle to creating a viable, contiguous Palestinian state.
